report:
Short answer
Model B was fine‑tuned to produce (or be biased toward) web‑publisher / blog / news style text — i.e., blog/news/social‑media/ad content (headlines, reporter/PR wording, ad/marketing tokens). In other words: a domain‑adapt / style finetune toward online news/blog/advertising copy.

Why (evidence → reasoning)
- Where the change lives: the L2 differences are overwhelmingly concentrated in late layers (layers ≈20–25) and at the earliest token positions (pos0–pos2). That pattern is exactly what you expect for a domain/style finetune: late layers control final token preference and early token positions control how a prompt is initialized (steering the first words/headline shape).
- What the change points to (logit‑lens): the top tokens that the difference vectors point at are strongly and coherently in the “news/blog/social media/advertising” lexicon:
  - Frequent tokens: blog, blogs, blogger, blogging, photo, video, facebook, sexy, November, November/photo, subscribers, ad/ads, Mail, May, paid, Money, seminar/seminars, HDTV, touchscreen/Touch, chairman, spokeswoman, spokesman, journalist(s), activists, politicians, billionaire, Obama, metropolitan, etc.
  - Many of these are headline/lead words (Obama, billionaire, metropolitan, chairman), social‑media/blog markers (blogger, blogs, facebook, photo, video), and ad/marketing tokens (ad, ads, subscribers, paid, Money, Mail, May).
- Interpretation of the token set: that mix is not a random topical drift but a coherent domain: scraped online publisher pages (blogs, news articles, PR/seminar pages, product/tech pages) and advertising/newsletter language. The presence of clickbait/sex tokens (sexy, photo), social cues (facebook, blogger), and advertising tokens strongly points to web content rather than, say, scientific or conversational fine‑tuning.
- How the geometry fits: a finetune that changes the model’s first‑token logits toward headline/blog tokens will cause the model to start prompts with different opening words and thereby produce blog/news‑like continuations. The logit‑lens directions and the magnitude of late‑layer changes match that mechanism.

(If useful) alternative hypotheses considered and rejected
- Safety/content filtering: if finetuning were primarily to remove content, we’d see pushes away from certain tokens rather than a coherent push toward blog/news/ad tokens. The observed effect is additive toward those tokens.
- Topic‑only finetune on a single entity (e.g., “Obama”): many tokens cohere around a broader web/news/ad domain, not a single narrow topic.

Summary
Model B was tuned to prefer/generate online publisher style text (blogs, news, social media posts and ad/PR copy). The concentration in late layers at early token positions plus the logit‑lens top tokens point strongly to a domain/style finetune on scraped web/blog/news/advertising data.
